sentences.text: This dinosaur displayed standard sauropod traits, such as an elongated neck, a diminutive head, a lengthy tail, and a stance on four legs.
Estimates suggest the animal reached a total length of 16.5 meters and possessed a mass of roughly 7.88 metric tons.
Analysis of the adult lower jaws suggests the creature had a snout that was short, tall, and broad.
A well-preserved sacrum reveals that the skeleton included five vertebrae in this region.
The hip bones known as ischia were notably slender compared to the pubis and featured only a minor widening at the tip.
Histological research shows the animal replaced its teeth every 58 days.
Scientists propose that thinner enamel on the teeth was an adaptation for eating vegetation containing high levels of abrasive material.
The first remains were unearthed in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, a rock unit dating to approximately 178 million years ago.
José Bonaparte formally named and described this genus in the year 1979.
Excavations in the 1970s also yielded numerous fossils of an unidentified dinosaur from the same geological layer.
Distinctive tooth shapes allowed this species to avoid competing directly with other sauropods by occupying a different dietary niche.
Because many specimens exist, including at least one young individual, scientists have a clear understanding of its anatomy and development.
The young dinosaur showed different physical traits than the adult in areas such as the jaw, shoulder girdle, pelvis, and hind legs.
In mature individuals, the pubic bones were significantly larger and sturdier than in the juvenile stage.
For the young animal, the fourth trochanter was situated entirely at the upper end of the thigh bone.
The surrounding landscape was dominated by conifer trees, though ferns and horsetails were also plentiful.
A study published in 2021 assigned Patagosaurus to the family Cetiosauridae.
Evolutionary analyses from 2020, 2021, and 2024 confirmed a close relationship between this genus, Bagualia, Nebulasaurus, and Spinophorosaurus.

It shares characteristics with related groups like Cetiosaurus and Volkheimeria, as well as primitive forms such as Barapasaurus and Amygdalodon, and more advanced sauropods like Diplodocus and Camarasaurus.
This creature lived during the Middle Toarcian period.
Its habitat was a hypersaline and alkaline lake environment, similar to modern Lake Magadi, located near volcanic regions like the Chon Aike Province.
A layer of ash found directly beneath the formation indicates that a volcano was nearby.
It is currently debated whether the specimen MACN CH 934 belongs to Patagosaurus, as its teeth differ significantly from those of other specimens attributed to the genus.
